lines.text: I woke up in a *falling* elevator.
lines.style: Young man in pure panic, shouting over a roaring wind while in free fall, breathless, the word falling stretched in terror.

lines.text: A hundred buttons. And *no* ground floor.
lines.style: Young man, shaken and breathing hard after a crash, quiet disbelief, the word no landing heavy.

lines.text: Just a sign: the doors stay open *thirty* seconds.
lines.style: Young man reading a sign aloud slowly, uneasy, a nervous swallow before the number.

lines.text: And someone before me... had been *counting.*
lines.style: Young man, a creeping whisper of dread, slow, the last word chilling.

lines.text: Welcome. Find Floor *Zero*, and you may leave.
lines.style: Calm, polite, unsettling announcer voice over an old intercom, smiling too much, slow and soft, like a hotel concierge who knows something terrible.
Young man, hushed and wary, eyes wide, the last word a confused whisper.

lines.text: Every drawing on the wall... was *me.*
lines.style: Young man, horrified realization building slowly, the last word barely a breath.
Young man, frozen, a sharp quiet gasp on the last word.

lines.text: She was holding a key. To Floor *zero.*
lines.style: Young man, whispering fast with a flash of hope, the last word electric.

lines.text: And behind her... something *huge* was coming.
lines.style: Young man, terrified whisper, trembling, the word huge swelling with fear.

lines.text: Ten seconds. Run for the key... or stay, and press *another* button?
lines.style: Young man, panicking, fast and desperate, torn between two choices, heart pounding.

lines.text: Comment *A* or *B.* You decide what I do.
lines.style: Young man, urgent and direct, speaking straight to the viewer, pleading but steady.

music.title: Floor 0 - Floor Twelve
music.style: Horror thriller score. Opens frantic: screaming rising strings and pounding low hits. Then a sudden silence, and a warped, detuned vintage elevator muzak melody on music box and electric piano, slowly sinking into a dark ambient drone with a ticking clock pulse, deep sub booms like giant footsteps, building tremolo strings and a racing heartbeat to a sudden cut. Instrumental only, no vocals, mixed to sit under a voiceover.
